newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh mounts rescue effort in cyclone areas.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh mounts rescue effort in cyclone areas.

text.p: Bangladesh launched a massive rescue and relief operation on Tuesday in areas ravaged by a severe cyclone that local newspapers said had killed hundreds of people.
Government officials said army, naval and police units joined thousands of volunteers and fanned out across coastal regions in the southeast of the country.

"But detailed estimates of losses of lives and property will not be available soon as many areas are still cut off after more than 200 kph (124 mph) winds, accompanied by rain, pounded the coast and offshore islands," said Golam Rabbani, director of Cyclone Preparedness Centre in the port city of Chittagong.
The cyclone, roaring in from the Bay of Bengal on Monday, ravaged Chittagong, the Cox's Bazar and Tenkaf districts and several islands, leaving a trail of devastation.
Foreign aid agencies including CARE International and Oxfam said their field workers had yet to send their first reports from places battered by the cyclone, which tapered off by midnight on Monday.
"They are still trying to get to the disaster scenes. We don't expect reports of casualties or damage from them until the afternoon," one CARE official in Dhaka said.
Officials on Tuesday said 13 people had died and more than 100 were injured, and said the figures would rise.
The Bangladesh Times, a government-run daily, reported on Tuesday that up to 500 people were feared killed in the cyclone.
Other newspapers, quoting their own sources, put the death toll at more than 350. More than 2,000 people were injured in Chittagong alone, they said.
Some 250 others had been killed in Cox's Bazar, one of the areas worst hit by the cyclone, the newspapers said.
About 100 fishermen from the coastal district of Patuakhali were missing at sea, newspaper reporters in Chittagong said.
"Most of the disaster-hit areas have not been accessed yet. It's very difficult to get a clear picture immediately," one official told Reuters.
A Navy vessel with relief supplies was sailing to Saint Martin's island which was inundated by a six-foot (two-metre) tidal surge on Monday.
Rescue and relief operations were hampered overnight by darkness and rough weather, relief ministry officials said.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was expected to visit the devastated areas on Tuesday, her aides said. Earlier she cancelled a planned visit to Spain in the wake of the cyclone.
Tens of thousands of houses were demolished and uprooted trees and power poles jammed roads in the worst affected areas. Power supplies and communications were cut in many places.
Chittagong port had suffered substantial damage, port officials said without giving details.
They said the fate of the Panamanian flagged ship Esco Argo, which sent an SOS message during the cyclone saying it was sinking in the Bay of Bengal near Kutubdia island, was still unclear.
Agriculture officials said there had been some damage to rice crops but shrimp cultivation was more seriously affected.
